summary:
Marswalk Map is an interactive, web-based tactical Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route planner designed for the first human missions to Mars. Focused on the astrobiologically rich Jezero Crater delta front, the system integrates seven NASA scientific datasets—including HiRISE high-resolution imagery, MOLA topographic slope models, CRISM mineral spectroscopy, THEMIS thermal inertia, and in-situ MEDA weather and RAD radiation telemetry from the Perseverance rover.

To address the challenge of surface exploration safety, Marswalk Map implements a multi-parameter A* pathfinding algorithm that dynamically weights steep slopes, boulder fields, and cumulative radiation exposure to compute the safest, most scientifically valuable routes between field sample targets. Crew members and mission planners can preview traverses on a global 3D CesiumJS globe or conduct interactive 3D mission rehearsals on a real-time Three.js tactical sandtable with first-person visor HUD telemetry. Marswalk Map bridges orbital remote sensing with ground operations to protect future Martian explorers.
details:
What Does It Do & How It Works

Marswalk Map is an interactive, browser-based tactical Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route planner engineered for future human exploration of the Jezero Crater delta front on Mars. The system acts as a high-precision navigational and safety briefing console, fusing 7 NASA datasets to evaluate terrain hazards and scientific opportunities simultaneously.

Users select scientific sample waypoints (e.g., hydrated silica outcrops, delta scarps, carbonate deposits) or choose pre-configured EVA scenarios. A hazard-weighted A* pathfinding algorithm calculates optimal traverse paths by evaluating terrain steepness (MOLA slope data), surface trafficability (THEMIS thermal inertia and boulder counts), and cumulative radiation exposure (Curiosity and Perseverance RAD data). Traversals can be examined on a global CesiumJS 3D globe or simulated in an interactive Three.js tactical sandtable that features an articulated NASA EMU astronaut walkthrough, dynamic camera modes (Orbital, Chase, and Visor POV), and real-time mission telemetry.

Key Benefits & Impact

- Crew Safety: Prevents traverses across high-risk terrain (>25° slopes, dust sinks, and boulder fields) while tracking cumulative radiation against the 1,000 µSv daily astronaut safety budget.

- Science Return: Optimizes traverse time and distance so crews maximize on-site sampling at high-priority astrobiological targets.

- Operational Pre-visualization: Provides ground control and astronaut crews with intuitive 3D sandtable briefings, reducing cognitive load before stepping onto the Martian surface.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software

- Frontend & 3D: React 18, TypeScript 5, Vite 5, CesiumJS 1.117, Three.js (r167), Tailwind CSS 3, Zustand 4.

- Data & Algorithms: Python 3.11, NumPy, custom multi-parameter A* pathfinding engine.

- Hosting & Infrastructure: Vercel (with serverless tile rewrites proxying NASA Trek APIs to bypass CORS).

Creativity & Mission Factors Considered

Rather than relying on flat 2D maps or passive simulations, Marswalk Map unifies macroscopic orbital remote sensing with ground-level astronaut perspectives (including Perseverance Mastcam-Z ground photography). It specifically accounts for spacesuit mobility constraints, solar lighting angles, diurnal thermal swings, and localized dust saltation dynamics.
